title: G4cube intro 01 pt1
speaker: Steve Jobs
content:
# G4cube intro 01 pt1

**Source**: /Volumes/NvME-Satechi/steve-jobs.ai/Database_Steve_Jobs/2000s/G4cube intro 01 pt1.mp4

**Transcribed**: 2025-12-31 11:24

---

**Speaker 1**: In first grade when I was painting with poster paints, I painted a boat and I made the smoke go the right direction and my first grade teacher told my mom, you should nurture his artistic ability. I've been a visual person ever since. Uh, I was an art director, I'm a designer and I just love how the cube looks. I mean, it's just the coolest looking computer on the planet.

**Speaker 2**: The first reaction I had to the size of the G4 Cube was really one of amazement because if you'd asked me in advance how small can a supercomputer be, uh, I never would have come close to what I saw.

**Speaker 3**: Three and a half gigaflops. Now that is three and a half billion operations per second. Um, it is staggering by any measure and 10 years ago it was unheard of in anything smaller than a washing machine.

**Speaker 4**: The heart of the G4 Cube is incredibly complex. I mean it's it's a supercomputer. But we were looking for a final design that was very simple. A design that left you with a sense of, well of course, that's the most natural, the most elegant solution possible.

**Speaker 5**: All the kind of functional characteristics are taken care of, but then there's another level of aesthetic that just lifts it and gives it spirit.

**Speaker 6**: Most computer companies would have said, this is an impossible task. They would have walked away from it. I mean to take a computer four times its size and pack it down into an 8-inch cube, it seems impossible, but we did it.

**Speaker 7**: Being this big and being able to sustain one, two, three or four gigaflops, we are looking at 2,000 times the volume efficiency of say a Cray supercomputer of the 1980s.

**Speaker 8**: The G4 Cube starts out with 64 megabytes of memory, expandable up to 1.5 gigabytes of RAM. It starts with a 20 gigabyte hard drive, configurable up to 40 gigabytes. It's got all the IO you could ever want. Ethernet, USB, Firewire, everything you need is in the cube.

**Speaker 9**: The Adobe users are going to love it. Um, it has everything they required. It has the power of a G4, but it has the elegance and the design element that they care about.

**Speaker 4**: The G4 Cube is designed to go onto your desk, so we saw that it was crucial that we could remove both visual and audible clutter. So the team figured out a way to actually remove the fan. The product's air cooled so that it's virtually silent.

**Speaker 5**: Instead of sitting down at a computer that's humming and and uh, and you kind of feel technology in the room, you're sitting down in the silence where you can sit and have an idea.

**Speaker 4**: The DVD has a nice element of surprise in the way that it rises from the top of the cube.
